interpretation_limits: Response bodies are absent; store_context_changed is source-based attribution, not a captured response code.
Compose output interleaves separately buffered services. Only timestamped mission-planner access entries are used to order or time events; backend duplicate access lines are not additional failures.

No browser record reads were logged during the idle interval. There is no claim of fresh-identity browser recovery immediately after deactivation. Without a manual mission_id, operatingMission selects no mission when deactivated, and useWorkspaceRecords requires a nonempty mission ID; that explains the idle pause from source.
Bounded observed browser recovery is after deliberate reactivation, within three seconds at access-log resolution, with the new identity matching the successful journal receipt.
The cancellation has no captured timestamp; it cannot be tied to the context transition from this evidence.

The browser harness counts all HTTP statuses >=400 except GPS 503 as failures, without context/body classification. Raw status failed and unexpected_failures=2 remain authoritative; this investigation does not establish an overall clean performance baseline.
No source changes, tests, services, runtime requests, or reruns were performed for this diagnosis.
